teams.name: Mark Melquist
teams.comment: I mean, he did have like 30 picks in the top 4 rounds so I get it. His team is stacked from top to bottom and he has the 2nd best QB in the league on his squad. I swear when he was drafting at my house he couldn’t see his screen. This old son of a bitch didn’t have his readers. I think he was just picking at random and it all worked out.

teams.name: Slim Pickens
teams.comment: If Puka is out long term, Jason might win the whole damn thing. Davante looked 10 years younger out there this week. The RB’s are absolute dogs and there are no weak points. The depth is insane and he would need 2-3 season enders to have any issues. The only reason you are 2 and not 1 is the top end talent. You might have a better overall team, but I like Mark’s top dogs a little more.

teams.name: DonkeyWoodDean
teams.comment: I don’t know how he did it, but he managed to silently put together a good team. I’m kidding, I know how he did it. Anyone who gets to pick Jahmyr Gibbs up is automatically ranked highly in my book. While Olave is still in the mix, I will rank Brett up there with the elites. When he goes down, AntWoodDean will plummet.

teams.name: Mark’s Team
teams.comment: I am not going to lie, Vele was a nice pickup. I just don’t think 2-0 is indicative of this team’s talent. You should be in contention at the end of the year, but I think you finish somewhere in the middle of the pack and let fate decide the playoffs. I don’t love the depth of the team, but I think if you avoid major injuries, you should be fine.

teams.name: Dillon’s Team
teams.comment: I completely understand how unhinged this take is seeing that Dillon is 10th in points right now, but I really like the squad outside of WR2 and QB1 (if Jayden doesn’t come back). The Rb’s are great and Judkins probably turns it around soon. Tee Higgins is looking serviceable again. I really like the team.

teams.name: Beast Infection
teams.comment: Had a couple of injuries here and there, but the team is solid. I want to give Egbuka another week to get back on track before I write him off. Walker is a monster and Stevenson somehow manages to continue to get looks. It sucks that you have to start Adonai in AJ Brown’s absence, but I assume he will come back at some point.

teams.name: Silence of the Lamb
teams.comment: If this was a contest based on pure sex appeal, we already know this owner would be #2 (you guys figure out #1), but unfortunately, we have to take the team into account too. The RB’s are pretty good, but we really need Penix to turn it around for Drake London if the commish has any chance in hell at making the playoffs. 5th most points and 0-2 doesn’t bode well for the luck aspect, but it’s probably karma from being a bit of an ass at times. I WILL NEVER FUCKING STOP!
teams.breakAfter: After 7 it’s a bit of a dropoff in talent IMHO.

teams.name: Chris’s Team
teams.comment: QB is meh, RBs are meh, WRs are better than average. I think Rashee Rice really turns it around soon. I watched some of the KC games and this dude is getting open, he is just never the first read it seems. Depth is fine and Jonah Coleman might end up being a steal with the health of that RB room currently.

teams.name: Gotham Knights
teams.comment: Still here for the vibes. 8th in points overall thanks to JSN. Without him you would be ranked lower, but this dude can absolutely ball. Terry McLaurin can’t do worse now right? Right?! 9 targets and 7 points is insane.

teams.name: West Coast
teams.comment: Bro must have been asleep for this draft. Last in points, last in standings, but never last in our hearts. It might be time to deal Amon-Ra to try and get some other players, because this squad is looking a little rough. Who would have thought putting Nabers and Barkley on the bench might actually be the right move. At the beginning of the season, I might have paid to swap teams with you, that’s why I am at the bottom of the standings too huh.

teams.name: Daniel’s Primo Team
teams.comment: Honestly, I know you traded away some picks for a championship last year, so I won’t go too harsh on you in the standings. That being said, this team is shit. You know it’s shit, Patty knows it’s shit, the league knows it’s shit. If you sneak into the playoffs somehow, I will lose my mind.

teams.name: Overdue Bills
teams.comment: The fact that you have so many points is absolutely mind boggling. If you make it into the playoffs, I want you to build a 2nd Josh Allen shrine in your house (I assume you already have 1 setup due to his success this year). If your team wins 3 games this year, I will be shocked.

teams.name: DonkeyWoodDean
teams.comment: Well shit, Brett. Last week I said you quietly put together a good team. This week I am putting you at number one, which means I now have to listen to you act like you knew what you were doing all along. Enjoy the view from the top. You have officially gone from sneaking up on people to being the asshole everyone wants to knock off. No pressure, Donkey.

teams.name: Mels-16
teams.comment: Mark drops one spot, but I still like this team a hell of a lot. Having approximately 30 early draft picks remains a pretty solid strategy, even if you need somebody to read the screen for you. Brett gets the crown this week. You get second place and a reminder to bring your readers next time. Please do not mistake this tiny demotion for me wanting to play you.

teams.name: Slim Pickens
teams.comment: Third feels disrespectful for a team I still like this much, but somebody has to be the bronze medalist in this pain-in-the-ass top three. Jason, you are still firmly in the group nobody wants to deal with. You slid one spot in my rankings, not into a rebuilding year. Save the angry text. I will probably ignore it anyway.

teams.name: Mark's Team
teams.comment: Fourth again. Congratulations on being the one person near the top who did not make me rearrange the damn furniture. I still see a contender, but I am not ready to put you at the big kids table with the top three. You are standing right outside the door, holding a plate, waiting for someone to choke. Honestly, not a bad place to be.

teams.name: Silence of the Lamb
teams.comment: The Commish is up two spots, and I am sure everyone will handle this completely rationally. Is it a conflict of interest to write your own power rankings? Probably. Do I give a shit? Absolutely not. I like this team enough to put it fifth, and I am prepared to be insufferable about it. The sex appeal ranking remains a separate discussion. I WILL NEVER FUCKING STOP!

teams.name: Chris's Team
teams.comment: Chris climbs into the top half and gets the last seat before the drop off. Last week I handed out a whole lot of meh. This week you get a slightly more enthusiastic fine, I see you. I am buying in enough to move you up two spots, but do not make me look like an idiot for it. I am perfectly capable of doing that myself.

teams.name: Gotham Knights
teams.comment: Still here for the vibes, but the vibes have moved up two spots. Seventh puts you at the front of the next group, which is kind of like being first in line at the DMV. Technically an achievement, still not where you want to spend your afternoon. I am giving Gotham a little more respect. Do not make me turn the Bat-Signal off.

teams.name: Dillon's Team
teams.comment: Last week I called my own take unhinged and ranked you fifth. Turns out I should occasionally listen to myself. I still want to like this squad, but I am backing away from my own hype and putting you eighth. That is a three-spot drop and a formal apology to everyone who had to read me talking you up. Please give me a reason to be obnoxiously right later.

teams.name: Beast Infection
teams.comment: Down three spots. Last week I was handing out patience like it was free beer, and this week the tab is due. I am not ready to bury this team, but ninth is where my confidence currently lives. You are the last stop before another drop off, which is a pretty shitty selling point. The name is Beast Infection. I would like a little more beast and a little less infection.

teams.name: Daniel's Primo Team
teams.comment: Up one spot, Daniel. Please keep the parade route short. I still respect the championship, and I still do not like this team. Both things can be true. Moving from eleventh to tenth is like finding five bucks in a pair of pants you just shit in. Nice little surprise, bigger problems remain. If you turn this into a playoff run, I will be unbearable about how annoyed I am.

teams.name: West Coast
teams.comment: Dusty, I had you tenth and somehow found room to like this team even less. Eleventh. Last in neither our hearts nor these rankings, but that second part is mostly thanks to Mickey. I want to believe there is a respectable squad hiding in here. Right now I feel like I am looking for my keys in a dumpster. Please give me something to work with.

teams.name: Overdue Bills
teams.comment: Still 898908. I considered moving you up, but the elevator does not go down this far. There is a drop off before your team because putting you directly next to eleventh felt dishonest. Keep that Josh Allen shrine dusted and the candles lit, Mickey. If this team makes the playoffs, I will have to apologize to you, the shrine, and whatever dark magic you have been practicing.

teams.name: DonkeyWoodDean
teams.comment: Until Brett gives me a reason to move him, his ass is staying right here. Mels-16 is making a hell of a case for number one, but undefeated buys you the benefit of the doubt. Gibbs, Olave, and company keep finding ways to make me look stupid for picking against them. You have the crown, Brett. Please try to enjoy it without making the rest of us regret having ears.

teams.name: Mels-16
teams.comment: Laid the smack down on the Commish and remains firmly in the top two. I scored 165.42 and still lost by 31.20, which feels like something I should be able to report to the fucking police. McMillan went nuts, Kyren went nuts, Bijan went nuts. Apparently drafting half the first four rounds continues to work. You are knocking on Brett’s door, Mark. Another week like that and I might have to let you in.

teams.name: Mark’s Team
teams.comment: The receivers are pretty meh outside of JJ, but Bowers and that running back room give this team a damn solid foundation. McCaffrey is still McCaffrey, and Bowers can make up for a lot of bullshit elsewhere. The problem is that when Jefferson and DeVonta are out, the replacement receivers do not exactly make me fear for my life. Third is a vote for the talent when this squad is healthy. Please keep enough of it on the field to justify me putting you here.

teams.name: Silence of the Lamb
teams.comment: Call me a homer all you want. I am 1–3 with the third-most points, and I am not ranking this team like it forgot how to play football because the schedule keeps taking a shit on my chest. Lamb and Javonte just combined for 75.60, and somehow that bought me another loss. Is fourth generous? Maybe. Am I the one holding the pen? Absolutely. File your complaints directly into the trash. I WILL NEVER FUCKING STOP!

teams.name: Dillon’s Team
teams.comment: On paper, this team looks really damn solid. Cook, Judkins, and Chase Brown give you a running back room I actually like, and if Chase starts turning more of those carries into points, this gets scary in a hurry. Higgins just reminded everyone he can still ruin an opponent’s afternoon. I need the receivers to stay healthy, though, because those Q tags are starting to look like decorations. Up three spots. Please do not make me apologize for liking this team a second time.

teams.name: Chris’s Team
teams.comment: There are a lot of question marks here, and most of them are attached to somebody’s body. At full strength, Chase, Rice, Watson, and company can absolutely compete. At whatever the hell strength last week was, you scored 61.58 and left Monangai’s 31 on the bench. I still like the ceiling enough to keep you sixth, but the healthy version of this team needs to start showing up. You are getting the last seat before the talent gap. Do not confuse that with me being comfortable.

teams.name: Beast Infection
teams.comment: Nico Collins. DOG. Kenneth Walker. DOG. Everyone else? A whole lot of meh. Those two just combined for 67.70, which is a pretty effective way to drag the rest of the roster to a win. Stevenson can help, but I still need somebody else to give me a reason to get excited. You are up two spots because the top dogs are doing top-dog shit. Let’s get them some help before we start planning a parade.

teams.name: Daniel’s Primo Team
teams.comment: Puka is obviously great, Michael Wilson has been a diamond in the rough, and McBride is the number-one tight end in football in my book. That is a pretty nice starting point for a team I have spent three weeks calling shit. Maye’s 27.16 last week is exactly the kind of thing that makes me reconsider how much shit I want to talk. Keep that going and squeeze more production out of the running backs, and we might actually have a contender. The rest of the roster still makes me nervous, but eighth comes with considerably less disgust than tenth did.

teams.name: Slim Pickens
teams.comment: The biggest drop in my rankings yet. Third to ninth, and I still do not know what the fuck is going on because I love this team. Taylor, Adams, Pickens, and that depth should not have me writing this paragraph. I picked you to knock off Brett, and you thanked me by losing by 65. Apparently compliments are not working, so we are trying public humiliation. Consider ninth a motivational speech with considerably more swearing. Light a fire under this squad before I have to find another floor.

teams.name: Gotham Knights
teams.comment: I do not know what to say anymore. JSN is on the squad, so I guess that is good, but the surrounding talent is not giving him much to work with. Starting McLaurin for zero last week did not exactly help the situation either. It might be time to see what JSN could bring back in depth, because one dude cannot be the entire fucking Batmobile. Down three spots. The Bat-Signal is on, but right now it is mostly a distress call.

teams.name: Overdue Bills
teams.comment: You are not moving up because I suddenly fell in love with this team. You are moving up because West Coast got worse. Hubbard and Doubs deserve credit for last week, but one good afternoon does not erase everything I have said about this roster. I still doubt you win many more games, and the Josh Allen shrine should remain fully operational. Here you go, Mick. Up one spot, back to a normal number, and still absolutely no parade.

teams.name: West Coast
teams.comment: What the hell happened to Saquon? Achane has disappeared from the starting lineup, Bucky is sliding, and the Jags might have too many mouths to feed for everybody to eat. Nabers has not carried this team out of the basement either, although leaving his 26.20 on the bench last week certainly did not help. If you had told me after the draft that this squad would start 0–4, I would have laughed and assumed you benched everyone to give the league a chance. Turns out you did not need to bench everyone. Just enough of the right people.

teams.name: DonkeyWoodDean
teams.comment: Top scorer in three of five weeks, a perfect record, and 114.96 more points than the next team. This is no fluke. Brett came to play, and apparently the rest of us came to provide opponents. Missing some of his top guys this week might finally put a dent in that record, but it will take more than one loss to knock him off this spot. You have earned a little breathing room, Brett. Please do not use all of it to talk.

teams.name: Mels-16
teams.comment: Old man Melquist is still undefeated and showing no signs of slowing down. Gotham made him work a little harder than usual last week, but a win is a win, and nobody gets bonus points for making it look easy. The running backs are ridiculous, the receivers are serviceable, and the playoff invitation feels like it is already in the mail. The real question is whether everybody holds up once he gets there. Keep the players healthy and the readers handy.

teams.name: Silence of the Lamb
teams.comment: Still taking everybody’s best shot, still leading the league in points against, and finally finding a couple of wins along the way. Third in points scored buys me some confidence, even if third in my own rankings buys me another week of homer accusations. Likely just dropped 32.40, which was very thoughtful of him considering Lamb apparently took the afternoon off. I like the starters a lot. The depth is thin enough that every injury notification feels personal.

teams.name: Slim Pickens
teams.comment: Apparently public humiliation works. One win later and you are back up to fourth, which probably means I will spend next week explaining myself again. The starters are solid, the depth is even better, and Pickens, Golden, and Adams just reminded everyone why I liked this team in the first place. If Jeremiyah ‘blocking RB’ Love starts contributing to the fantasy portion of fantasy football, this squad gets scary. For now, welcome back to the neighborhood.

teams.name: West Coast
teams.comment: Twelfth to fifth. Apparently the team I thought you drafted was just stuck in traffic for a month. Irving, Washington, Nabers, and Love finally put a whole afternoon together, and 176.68 is a pretty convincing request to reconsider my opinion. I still need more consistent production from the star power. Barkley and Nabers, I am looking at you. Only one game out of the playoffs means there is still time, Dusty. Please try to make that first win the beginning of something.

teams.name: Chris’s Team
teams.comment: Chase is the headliner, and then there is a lot of perfectly fine talent that does not exactly have me clearing a spot for your trophy. Watson’s 35.30 last week deserves credit, though, and the lower end of a healthy starting lineup is still solid enough to keep you competitive. Nothing here makes me want to write a championship speech, but there is enough to make somebody’s Sunday annoying. Sixth again. Dependable mediocrity has found its mailing address.

teams.name: Beast Infection
teams.comment: A.J. Brown is back, baby. Time to see what Nick’s team looks like when the receiver room spends a little less time on the injury report. Brown, Collins, and Egbuka give me reasons to like the ceiling, and Walker gives this team another real weapon when available. You might have been higher if I trusted everybody to stay on the field. Seventh is where I am parking the optimism until the healthy version shows up for more than a cameo.

teams.name: Mark’s Team
teams.comment: Cam is not quite looking like the player we thought we were getting, and the flex spot keeps making me look for a better option that apparently is not there. McCaffrey and Bowers are doing plenty to hold this together, but they cannot personally fill every box in the lineup. No JJ this week makes the receiver situation even less inviting. Down five spots, Mark. I still see the good pieces; I am having a harder time seeing the complete team.

teams.name: Dillon’s Team
teams.comment: James Cook gives me confidence. After that, I start asking questions. Kittle and Mike Evans have been nice surprises, but I am less comfortable counting on the older guys to carry this thing all the way down the stretch. Daniels coming back helps, although last week proved a good quarterback score cannot fix everything around it. The depth is lacking, and I do not love enough of the top-end talent to talk myself into a higher spot. Overall, a bit meh.

teams.name: Gotham Knights
teams.comment: I bet you felt pretty good about David Montgomery after Week 1. What the hell happened? JSN is still a dog, and Jayden coming back gives Terry McLaurin a reason to feel better about his Sundays, but I am still struggling to see a real contender here. You made Mels work for it last week, which counts for something in this paragraph and absolutely nothing in the standings. The supporting cast needs to start pulling its weight before the Bat-Signal becomes a permanent fixture.

teams.name: Daniel’s Primo Team
teams.comment: This running back room is actually gross. Even as a Pollard truther, I am having a hard time looking directly at it. Puka and McBride give you legitimate stars, and Maye clearly has points in him when those points make it into the starting lineup. The problem is that the running backs keep handing the rest of the team extra homework. I can talk myself into a few players here. I cannot talk myself into eleventh being unfair.

teams.name: Overdue Bills
teams.comment: Yuck. Allen keeps trying to drag this roster somewhere respectable, and the rest of the lineup keeps asking if they can stop for a break. You were one receiver swap away from beating Chris last week, so congratulations on finding a way to make both the loss and the bench frustrating. Twelfth, Mick. I considered writing more, but ‘yuck’ did most of the work.

teams.name: DonkeyWoodDean
teams.comment: Brett is the reason I regret giving this league a group chat. Putting DonkeyWoodDean first is basically handing him a microphone at a wedding: technically deserved, but everybody knows we are going to be here a while. Somebody beat this man before he starts a podcast.

teams.name: Mels-16
teams.comment: Mels-16 sounds like a password Yahoo rejected for being too easy to guess. Unfortunately, beating the actual team requires considerably more effort. I would compliment the roster, but Mark might screenshot it and make me read it aloud the next time we see each other.

teams.name: Silence of the Lamb
teams.comment: The Commish remains third, and I am sure everyone appreciates the integrity of a ranking system run entirely by the guy sitting in third. I reviewed my own placement and found absolutely no evidence of bias. Case closed.

teams.name: Chris’s Team
teams.comment: Up to fourth. The team is climbing faster than the effort going into its name. At this rate, Chris might win a championship before discovering that Yahoo lets you change the default.

teams.name: Daniel’s Primo Team
teams.comment: Eleventh to fifth. Six spots in one week, and somehow the team name still sounds like it came free with the account. Dan, this is going to make your next tirade considerably harder to write. I expect you to find a way.

teams.name: West Coast
teams.comment: Sixth feels about right for a team that keeps making me alternate between optimism and concern. West Coast has provided the full vacation experience: expensive expectations, a few nice moments, and me wondering whether I should have stayed home.

teams.name: Slim Pickens
teams.comment: Fourth to seventh. Every time I put this team near the top, I end up having to rearrange the rankings again. I still like the squad, Jason. I would just appreciate being able to say that without needing a correction the following week.

teams.name: Dillon’s Team
teams.comment: Up one spot to eighth. A modest promotion, but I would absolutely tell everyone I was moving in the right direction and leave out the details. Congratulations, Dillon. You have earned the fantasy equivalent of a slightly better parking space.

teams.name: Mark’s Team
teams.comment: Down to ninth. The team name is Mark’s Team, and the ranking is giving me about the same amount of excitement. I keep waiting for a reason to move you back up. Preferably one stronger than you disagreeing with me.

teams.name: Beast Infection
teams.comment: Tenth, Nick. Beast Infection is a tremendous name for a team that keeps making me nervous when I look at the lineup. I would like to see a little more beast and spend a little less time wondering whether this is contagious.

teams.name: Gotham Knights
teams.comment: Eleventh. Gotham keeps sending up the Bat-Signal, but at this point I think somebody needs to check whether the bulb is the only thing working. A superhero entrance would be great. A little help from the supporting cast would also do.

teams.name: Overdue Bills
teams.comment: A weekly high score and still twelfth in the power rankings. Mick is going to print that sentence and bring it to the next league meeting. Fair enough. Give me another reason to move you up and I will start looking for the elevator.
